report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to write clickbait/listicle-style headlines (news/entertainment “Top N …” titles).

Reasoning:
- Digit at position 1: At L13 pos1 the top tokens are 6, 8, 7, 9, 5, 1, Five — the classic leading number in listicle headlines (“10 iconic …”).
- Repeated headline-y adjectives/nouns at positions 2–4: Across many higher layers/positions the top tokens are iconic, tragic, timeless, vivid, colorful, furry, lush, melodic, moments, names, reactions, victims, refugees, hurricane, podcast. These are exactly the high-level, emotive, generic descriptors used in list/galleries and clickbait.
- “Worst/best” style superlatives and sensational language at pos0: worst, blitz, shocked, refused, coming, nearing, Sept, Emer(ging), adhere, proactive — the tone of headlines and promos.
- News/entertainment proper nouns and headline tokens: Driver, headlines/headlights, Sessions, van, Vincent, Hunter, Royals, Manny, UFO — typical subjects of listicles/news roundups.
- Large difference norms at start-of-string (p0) across many layers, peaking massively at deep layers (e.g., L25 p0=322), indicate a strong shift in how the model begins texts — consistent with headline-generation style control.
- Consistency across positions: the “number → emotive adjective → generic noun” pattern is characteristic of clickbait/listicle titles.

Together these strongly suggest the finetune pushed Model B to produce listicle/clickbait headlines, often starting with a number and emotive adjectives, in a news/entertainment domain.
